newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing for first-time jobless benefits fell last week to the lowest level in a month, the government said Thursday.
The Labour Department reported that initial jobless claims in the week ended June 21 dropped to 332,000, down from 346,000 the week before.
Wall Street economists surveyed by Reuters had expected claims of 340,000.
Claims had been climbing steadily over the course of the previous few weeks. So even with a drop in claims last week, the four-week average of claims rose to its highest level in five months.
The average, which gives economists a more reliable view of trends in the labour market, jumped to 338,750 last week from 335,250 the week before.
The latest figure was at its highest level since the week ended Jan. 25, when the average reached 339,750.
The number of people continuing to claim benefits rose by 42,000 to 2,308,000 in the week ended June 14, the latest week for which data were available.
That was up from a revised 2,266,000 the week earlier.
